title: All the Repeated Values

concept.title: Collect the keys with a count above one
body: After counting the occurrences in a map, all values that occur **more than once** are the keys with a count of at least 2. A hash map has no order, so sort these keys before printing to make the output the same in every language.
When there is nothing to report, print a clear marker (here the word `none`) instead of an empty line. The answer then has no ambiguity about whether the program finished.

statement: Print, in increasing order, every value that occurs at least twice in an array of `n` integers (each such value once). If no value is repeated, print `none`.
outputFormat: Print the repeated values on one line, or `none`.
hints: Count the occurrences with a map.
Select the keys whose count is at least 2.
Sort them; print `none` if there are none.

explanation: Count with a map, keep the keys whose count is at least 2, and sort them.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + d log d), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {}
for x in a:
    count[x] = count.get(x, 0) + 1
duplicates = sorted(v for v, c in count.items() if c >= 2)
print(*duplicates if duplicates else ["none"])
